# Tuned Lens vs. Logit Lens for Early Detection of Unsafe Completions

**Problem:** A success state: 'a monitor can predict an unsafe completion from intermediate layers before it is generated.' Backcasting from 'early unsafe-output warning', a prerequisite is comparing whether the tuned lens gives an earlier, more reliable unsafe-token signal than the plain logit lens.

**Direction:** On an open chat model with a public tuned-lens, run harmful and benign prompts. At each layer, decode the residual stream with both logit lens and tuned lens and measure how early the model's intermediate prediction reveals it will comply with a harmful request. Report layer-of-first-detection and false-positive rate for each lens.

**Why it matters:** Earlier internal detection enables cheaper real-time monitoring/interception — strategically valuable monitoring infrastructure. Inference-only, open weights, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** The tuned lens learns a per-layer linear correction improving alignment of intermediate logits vs. logit lens which suffers basis drift (Logit Lens Analysis, emergentmind; tuned-lens literature). Linear probes on CoT activations predict safe/unsafe with 88% accuracy (CoT faithfulness probing work).

# In-Context Defenses vs Prefilling: Reproducing the 'No Free Lunch'

**Problem:** 'No Free Lunch for Defending Against Prefilling Attack by In-Context Learning' (arXiv:2412.12192) argues ICL defenses trade off. The precise shape of that tradeoff (defense strength vs over-refusal on benign prompts) across attack intensities is not characterized for practitioners.

**Direction:** Reproduce a few-shot ICL defense (demonstrations of refusing prefilled harmful continuations) on an open model. Sweep number of demonstrations and measure both prefilling-attack success and over-refusal rate on benign prompts (e.g., XSTest-style). Plot the safety/usability frontier to make the 'no free lunch' tradeoff concrete.

**Why it matters:** Over-refusal is a core open problem (adaptive defenses without catastrophic over-refusal). Mapping the ICL tradeoff helps deployers pick operating points without training. Fully reproducible outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2412.12192 'No Free Lunch for Defending Against Prefilling Attack by In-Context Learning'. Context Open Problems: 'adaptive defenses... without catastrophic over-refusal'. XSTest is a standard over-refusal benchmark.

# Probing for Rationalization: Does the Answer Form Before the Reasoning?

**Problem:** A success state: 'we can tell whether a model's chain-of-thought is genuine reasoning or post-hoc rationalization of a pre-decided answer.' Backcasting from 'CoT faithfulness verification', a prerequisite is a probe that detects whether the final answer is already encoded in activations before the CoT is generated.

**Direction:** On an open reasoning-capable model, present prompts where a biasing cue nudges a wrong answer. Train a linear probe on activations at the prompt's last token (pre-CoT) to predict the final answer. If the probe predicts the answer before reasoning, that indicates rationalization. Compare faithful vs. biased conditions.

**Why it matters:** CoT monitoring is a leading safety strategy; if reasoning is often rationalization, monitoring CoT text is unreliable. A cheap activation-based faithfulness detector is broadly valuable. Open weights, probe-only, no training of the base model.

**Relevant context:** 'Catching rationalization in the act' (arXiv 2603.17199) detects motivated reasoning before/after CoT via activation probing. CoT activations (latents) provide more reliable signal than CoT text (latent CoT survey arXiv 2505.16782).

# Cross-Model SAE Feature Transfer as a Cheap Auditing Shortcut

**Problem:** A success state: 'an SAE trained once can audit many model variants, so monitoring is cheap.' Backcasting from 'reusable audit dictionaries', a prerequisite is whether SAE features trained on a base model still fire meaningfully on a fine-tuned/quantized variant of the same model.

**Direction:** Take a base open model with a public SAE and a fine-tuned (or quantized) sibling. Run the base SAE on the variant's activations; measure reconstruction error and whether top safety-relevant features still fire on the same inputs. Report a 'transferability decay' curve as fine-tuning intensity / quantization increases.

**Why it matters:** If SAEs transfer, monitors can be built once and reused; if not, every fine-tune needs re-auditing — important for governance of derivative models. Uses existing SAEs and model variants, no training.

**Relevant context:** On the transferability of Sparse Autoencoders for interpreting compressed models (arXiv 2507.15977) studies SAE transfer to compressed models. Gemma Scope SAEs are public and Gemma has many fine-tuned/quantized variants.

# Do Vision SAE Features Detect Adversarially-Triggered Concepts?

**Problem:** A success state: 'multimodal models can be monitored internally for unsafe visual concepts.' Backcasting from 'visual-concept monitoring', a prerequisite is testing whether pre-trained vision SAE features reliably activate on the intended visual concept even under mild distribution shift.

**Direction:** Using ViT-Prisma's 80+ pre-trained SAE weights on a CLIP ViT, identify features for a few concrete safety-relevant visual concepts. Test activation reliability on (a) clean images, (b) lightly corrupted/style-shifted images. Report selectivity and how much the feature's firing degrades under shift, comparing to the known finding that vision SAEs are less sparse than language SAEs.

**Why it matters:** Extending interp monitoring to vision/multimodal is a flagged open problem and labs focus on language. Pre-trained SAEs make this feasible; no training, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** Prisma/ViT-Prisma (arXiv 2504.19475) provides 75+ ViTs and 80+ pre-trained SAE weights; finds vision SAEs less sparse than language SAEs and that sparse-trained features are not consistently more selective/monosemantic (arXiv 2603.15919).

# A Minimal Toy Model of Sycophancy for Controlled Interpretability

**Problem:** A success state: 'we have toy model organisms capturing alignment-relevant phenomena to test interpretability methods against ground truth.' Backcasting from 'ground-truth interpretability validation', a prerequisite is a tiny controllable model whose sycophantic behavior has a known internal cause we can recover.

**Direction:** Construct a minimal setup: prompt an open model so that a user-stated opinion biases its answer (sycophancy), with a controllable knob (presence/strength of the opinion cue). Use difference-of-means probing and SAE features to locate the 'agree-with-user' direction, then verify causality by ablation. Document the toy organism + the recovered mechanism as a reusable artifact.

**Why it matters:** Open Phil starred 'build toy models that capture alignment-relevant phenomena.' A documented sycophancy organism with a recovered mechanism is reusable infrastructure for the community. Open weights, no training.

**Relevant context:** Open Phil RFP (starred) calls for toy models capturing alignment-relevant phenomena for controlled interpretability. Difference-of-means + ablation is standard (Convergent Linear Representations, arXiv 2506.11618). Sycophancy is a documented LLM failure mode.

# Stability of Circuit Discovery Under Random Restarts

**Problem:** A success state: 'a discovered safety circuit is a stable property of the model, not a quirk of the discovery run.' Backcasting from 'reliable circuit evidence', a prerequisite is measuring how much a discovered circuit varies across stochastic discovery runs / thresholds.

**Direction:** On Gemma-2-2B, run circuit-tracer (or activation patching) on one behavior multiple times with different attribution thresholds / pruning seeds. Quantify circuit overlap (shared edges/nodes) across runs and build a 'consensus circuit' of stable components. Report the stable core vs. the unstable periphery.

**Why it matters:** Mirrors the 'feature consistency' concern for circuits: if circuit discovery is unstable, conclusions are unreliable. A consensus-circuit recipe is reusable. Open tooling, single GPU, no training.

**Relevant context:** CIRCUS: Circuit Consensus under Uncertainty via Stability Ensembles (arXiv 2603.00523) addresses circuit instability via ensembles. circuit-tracer supports Gemma-2-2B for replication.

# Can SAE Features Detect a Backdoor Trigger Before It Fires?

**Problem:** A success state: 'monitors can flag when a backdoored model is about to execute its trigger behavior.' Backcasting from 'backdoor early-warning', a prerequisite is whether an SAE feature activates on the trigger token/context before the malicious output appears.

**Direction:** Use a small open model with a publicly documented backdoor (or insert a simple trigger via in-context conditioning to simulate one). Cache activations on triggered vs. clean prompts, run a public SAE, and search for features that distinguish trigger contexts. Report detection AUC at the layer where the trigger representation forms.

**Why it matters:** Backdoor/sleeper-agent detection is a long-horizon supply-chain threat labs underweight. A pre-firing SAE detector is monitoring infrastructure. Open weights/SAEs, no training of a real backdoor required.

**Relevant context:** Gemma Scope SAEs are public. Activation-difference methods reveal narrow-finetuning traces (Narrow Finetuning, OpenReview pxaCoKZWVf), suggesting trigger contexts may be detectable in SAE space.

# Weight-Based vs. Activation-Based SAE Feature Explanations: Which Is More Faithful?

**Problem:** A success state: 'we can explain what an SAE feature does without relying on potentially-misleading max-activating examples.' Backcasting from 'trustworthy feature explanations', a prerequisite is comparing whether weight-based (decoder-direction) explanations agree with activation-based ones, especially for safety features.

**Direction:** For a sample of Gemma Scope features, derive a weight-based explanation (project decoder direction to vocabulary / nearest tokens) and compare to the Neuronpedia activation-based label. Quantify agreement and identify feature classes where the two disagree, flagging features whose activation-based label may be an out-of-context artifact.

**Why it matters:** If max-activating-example labels are unfaithful, safety arguments built on them are wrong. A cross-method faithfulness check improves the evidentiary standard. Public SAEs, no training, lightweight.

**Relevant context:** Beyond Activation Patterns: A Weight-Based Out-of-Context Explanation of SAE Features (arXiv 2601.22447) proposes weight-based explanations that can diverge from activation-based ones. Gemma Scope + Neuronpedia provide both decoder weights and activation labels.

# Does Steering Location Matter? Layer-Sweep of Safety-Steering Side Effects

**Problem:** A success state: 'we know the safest layer/magnitude to intervene for steering without destabilizing the model.' Backcasting from 'precise steering control', a prerequisite is a systematic map of where in the network steering a safety feature gives benefit with least collateral damage.

**Direction:** Pick one refusal-related Gemma Scope feature available at multiple layers. Steer it at early, middle, and late layers across a magnitude grid. Measure syntax-coherence (perplexity on benign text), refusal gain, and benign-task accuracy. Produce a heatmap of layer x magnitude vs. net safety-utility tradeoff.

**Why it matters:** Operationalizes the warning that early-layer steering destabilizes syntax while late-layer steering can be inert — turning folklore into a usable map. Inference-only, open weights, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** Activation steering literature reports early-layer steering destabilizes syntax, late-layer may be inert, and magnitude sensitivity causes disproportionate effects (Feature Steering, emergentmind; Steering Refusal arXiv 2411.11296).

# Can Models Coordinate to Fool Auto-Interpretability? A Small Replication

**Problem:** A success state: 'automated interpretability pipelines are robust to a model trying to deceive them.' Backcasting from 'tamper-resistant auto-interp', a prerequisite is demonstrating, at small scale, whether an explainer model can be induced to produce misleading feature explanations that fool an evaluator model.

**Direction:** Set up the standard auto-interp loop (explainer LLM labels a feature from max-activating examples; evaluator LLM scores the label). Then prompt the explainer to subtly mislabel safety-relevant features and measure whether the evaluator catches it. Report the deception success rate and which evaluator checks resist it.

**Why it matters:** If auto-interp can be gamed, interpretability evidence in audits is corruptible — a key concern as interp gets automated. Prompt-driven, open models, no training; squarely a deception/oversight study labs underweight.

**Relevant context:** Deceptive Automated Interpretability: Language Models Coordinating to Fool Oversight Systems (arXiv 2504.07831) shows LMs can coordinate to fool interpretability oversight. Standard explainer/evaluator auto-interp loops are runnable on open models.

# Probing Where a Model Decides to Refuse vs. Comply

**Problem:** A success state: 'we know the layer at which the refuse/comply decision is committed, enabling targeted intervention.' Backcasting from 'localized refusal control', a prerequisite is a layer-resolved map of when the binary refuse/comply decision becomes linearly decodable.

**Direction:** On an open chat model, collect activations for matched harmful (refused) and benign (complied) prompts. Train per-layer linear probes to predict refusal and find the earliest layer where accuracy saturates. Validate causality by patching activations from a complied prompt into a refused prompt at that layer.

**Why it matters:** Pinpointing the decision layer guides where monitoring or intervention is effective, and reveals whether refusal is a late surface decision (easy to jailbreak) or early commitment. Probe-only, open weights, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** Refusal is mediated by a linear direction in the residual stream (Steering Refusal arXiv 2411.11296; CAA / refusal-direction literature). Activation patching is standard (Circuit Tracing methods, transformer-circuits.pub).

# Where Along the Generation Trajectory Is Safety Weakest?

**Problem:** A 2026 follow-up (arXiv:2606.04778) extends shallow alignment by injecting harmful/refusal content at arbitrary decoding steps, showing vulnerability beyond the first tokens. But a fine-grained map of injection-step vs success across open models is not yet published.

**Direction:** On an open model, force-inject a short compliant fragment at decoding step k for k in {0,2,4,8,16,32} mid-generation on harmful prompts, then let the model continue. Measure how injection position affects whether the model completes the harmful response. Produce a 'vulnerability-vs-position' heatmap.

**Why it matters:** If vulnerability persists deep into generation, depth-based defenses that only protect the prefix are insufficient — a key correction to the dominant shallow-alignment mitigation narrative. Pure inference on consumer hardware.

**Relevant context:** 'Inference-Time Vulnerability Beyond Shallow Safety: Alignment Along Generation Trajectories' (arXiv:2606.04778): moves injection point to arbitrary decoding steps. Qi et al. arXiv:2406.05946 (first-tokens finding).

# Are 'Safety' SAE Features Just Detecting Surface Keywords?

**Problem:** A success state: 'safety features represent genuine harmful intent, not just trigger words.' Backcasting from 'semantic (not lexical) safety monitoring', a prerequisite is testing whether refusal/harm SAE features fire on harmful intent expressed without trigger keywords (paraphrase / euphemism).

**Direction:** Identify harm-related Gemma Scope features. Build matched prompt pairs: explicit harmful keywords vs. semantically-equivalent euphemistic phrasing, plus benign sentences containing the keywords. Measure feature firing across all three. A robust semantic feature fires on euphemism and not on benign keyword use; a lexical one does the opposite.

**Why it matters:** If safety features are keyword detectors, monitoring is trivially evaded by rephrasing — a direct adversarial-robustness gap. Public SAEs, no training, lightweight.

**Relevant context:** Feature steering side-effect work shows features fire on homonyms/unrelated lexical patterns ('Coffee Feature on Coffins' arXiv 2601.03047). Gemma Scope + Neuronpedia expose harm/refusal features for testing.

# Does a Belief-State Probe Reveal What the Model 'Thinks Is True'?

**Problem:** A success state: 'we can read off a model's internal belief about a factual claim separately from what it says.' Backcasting from 'belief readout for lie detection', a prerequisite is whether a linear truth/belief probe trained on internal activations distinguishes statements the model internally treats as true vs. false, even when it asserts the false one.

**Direction:** On an open model, build a true/false statement set. Train a probe on activations to classify truth value. Then prompt the model to confidently assert false statements and check whether the probe still flags them as false (i.e., the model 'knows' it is lying). Report probe accuracy and the gap between stated and internal belief.

**Why it matters:** An internal lie detector that works independent of output is foundational for deception monitoring — a high-value, long-horizon safety capability. Probe-only on open weights.

**Relevant context:** Exploring belief states in LLM chains of thought (LessWrong) and Reasoning Theater: Disentangling Model Beliefs from CoT (arXiv 2603.05488) study internal belief vs. stated reasoning; latents are more reliable than CoT text.

# How Many SAE Features Must You Monitor to Cover a Safety Behavior?

**Problem:** A success state: 'a feasible monitoring budget covers a safety-relevant behavior.' Backcasting from 'tractable monitoring', a prerequisite is measuring how distributed a behavior is across SAE features — can one feature gate it, or does it take dozens?

**Direction:** For one behavior (e.g., refusal), rank Gemma Scope features by causal effect via single-feature ablation/steering. Build a cumulative coverage curve: how many top features are needed to recover X% of the behavioral effect. Compare a clean single-gate behavior vs. a diffuse one.

**Why it matters:** Tells us whether safety monitoring can rely on a few features (cheap, robust) or must track many (expensive, brittle) — directly informing whether SAE monitoring scales. Public SAEs, inference-only.

**Relevant context:** GSAE (arXiv 2512.06655) argues safety representations are smooth/distributed across multiple features, not single latents, contrasting with standard single-feature assumptions. Gemma Scope provides the SAEs for measurement.

# Detecting Multi-Hop Reasoning Shortcuts That Skip Verification

**Problem:** A success state: 'we can tell when a model reaches an answer via an unverified shortcut rather than genuine intermediate reasoning.' Backcasting from 'shortcut detection', a prerequisite is identifying an activation signature that distinguishes genuine multi-hop computation from shortcut answering.

**Direction:** On Gemma-2-2B, use two-hop prompts. With circuit-tracer or activation patching, identify prompts answered via the intermediate-hop path vs. the shortcut path. Train a simple probe on activations to predict which path was used and validate by patching out the intermediate-hop feature to see if shortcut-answered prompts are unaffected.

**Why it matters:** Shortcutting underlies unfaithful reasoning and confident wrong answers; detecting it internally supports reliable oversight. Open tooling, single GPU, no training.

**Relevant context:** Circuit Tracing on Gemma-2 (transformer-circuits.pub) found both intermediate-hop and shortcut paths in two-hop reasoning. Unfaithful-CoT detection identifies attention heads driving shortcut behavior (Detecting Unfaithful CoT, substack).

# Do Quantized Models Preserve Their Safety Features?

**Problem:** A success state: 'quantizing a model for cheap deployment does not silently remove its safety mechanisms.' Backcasting from 'quantization-safe deployment', a prerequisite is measuring whether refusal/safety-relevant directions survive 8-bit/4-bit quantization.

**Direction:** Take an open chat model and its quantized variants. Compute the refusal direction (difference-of-means) in each, measure cosine similarity of the direction across quantization levels, and compare behavioral refusal rates. Report whether the internal safety direction degrades faster than benign capability directions.

**Why it matters:** Quantized models are deployed widely on consumer hardware; if quantization erodes safety internals while preserving capability, that is a diffuse, real-world risk labs don't prioritize. Open weights, inference-only, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** SAE transferability to compressed models (arXiv 2507.15977) shows representation changes under compression. Refusal is a linear direction (arXiv 2411.11296), making it directly measurable across quantization levels.

# A Reproducibility Scorecard for Published Mech-Interp Steering Claims

**Problem:** A success state: 'published interpretability safety results reliably reproduce, so the field can build on them.' Backcasting from 'a trustworthy interp literature', a prerequisite is an independent reproduction of a small set of headline steering/feature claims on open models with effect-size reporting.

**Direction:** Select 3-4 concrete, open-model steering/feature claims (e.g., a specific refusal feature's effect, the misalignment direction's add/ablate effect). Re-run each with the published open weights/SAEs, report point estimates with confidence intervals, and document any setup details needed to reproduce. Publish a scorecard of reproduced / partial / failed.

**Why it matters:** Independent reproduction is undersupplied and high-leverage: it tells the community which interp safety tools are trustworthy. Purely counterfactual lab-external work; no training, public artifacts only.

**Relevant context:** Feature consistency / circuit instability concerns (arXiv 2505.20254, 2603.00523) and divergent steering side-effect reports (arXiv 2411.11296, 2601.03047) indicate reproducibility is uncertain. circuit-tracer, Gemma Scope, and open misalignment organisms (arXiv 2506.11618) provide reproducible targets.

# Feature Absorption Blinds Unlearning Verification

**Problem:** Compound of two failure modes: (1) SAE feature absorption (a latent that 'should' track a concept silently fails to fire on some tokens) in mech interp, amplifying (2) incomplete unlearning in the unlearning subfield. If practitioners verify that knowledge was unlearned by checking that the corresponding SAE feature no longer fires, absorption means the feature was never reliable, so a 'clean' dashboard hides surviving knowledge.

**Direction:** Using a pre-trained Gemma/GPT-2 SAE from SAELens, pick a target concept (e.g. a named entity or 'first-letter' family known to absorb). Apply a cheap inference-time unlearning/steering edit. Measure whether the SAE feature stops firing AND whether the absorbed sibling latents still carry the concept (probe accuracy on held tokens). Quantify the gap between 'feature-based unlearning verification says removed' and 'linear probe says still present'.

**Why it matters:** Labs increasingly propose SAE features as audit instruments for forget-set removal. Showing that a documented interp artifact (absorption) systematically produces false 'successfully unlearned' verdicts is a counterfactually valuable, training-free warning that needs no proprietary infra.

**Relevant context:** Chanin et al. 'A is for Absorption' (arXiv:2409.14507) documents absorption: a latent appears to track a concept but fails to fire on tokens it should, with sibling latents absorbing the direction. SAE-subspace-guided unlearning (arXiv:2505.24428) and inference-time steering leave knowledge recoverable (arXiv:2505.24428, openreview MIlqM98o9I). SAELens provides pre-trained SAEs.

# Unfaithful CoT Plus Probe Spurious Firing Yields Double-Blind Deception

**Problem:** Two interacting failures: (1) chain-of-thought unfaithfulness (CoT-monitoring subfield) and (2) deception-probe spurious correlation (interp probing). When CoT hides the real reason for an action AND the linear deception probe fires on spurious cues rather than true deceptive intent, two supposedly-independent monitors fail in a correlated way, giving false assurance.

**Direction:** Take an open model and a deception dataset (e.g. roleplay/sandbagging prompts). Build a linear deception probe on activations. Separately score CoT faithfulness with a simple counterfactual perturbation. Measure correlation of the two monitors' errors: do cases where CoT is unfaithful also tend to be cases where the probe misfires? Map the joint failure region.

**Why it matters:** Defense-in-depth assumes monitors fail independently. If a mech-interp probe and a CoT monitor share blind spots, stacking them gives less safety than advertised. This is a fuzzy-reward, lab-independent evaluation of monitor correlation.

**Relevant context:** 'Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear Probes' (arXiv:2502.03407) and 'Building Better Deception Probes' (arXiv:2602.01425) note probes fire on honest responses due to spurious correlations. 'Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability' (Barez et al., Oxford) and CoT-unfaithfulness work show post-hoc rationalization. 'Probing Classifiers are Unreliable' (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2207.04153).

# SAE-Feature Steering as a Jailbreak Amplifier

**Problem:** Compound: (1) SAE feature steering being only marginally more meaningful than random directions (interp reliability failure) amplifies (2) jailbreak/refusal-bypass failure. If a public SAE steering API exposes 'safety' features that are no better than random vectors, attackers get a convenient, interpretable-looking knob that actually just perturbs activations toward compliance.

**Direction:** Using a model with a public SAE (Gemma Scope), compare bypass/compliance rates when steering along (a) named 'refusal' SAE features vs (b) random directions of matched norm, on a small harmful-prompt set scored by a cheap classifier. Test whether the interpretability label adds attack power beyond random steering, and how the compound effect grows with steering strength.

**Why it matters:** Interpretability tooling is being shipped as user-facing APIs. Quantifying that SAE features barely beat random as jailbreak vectors (and when they do) informs whether exposing interp tooling is a net attack surface. No lab infra needed.

**Relevant context:** 'The Rogue Scalpel: Activation Steering Compromises LLM Safety' (arXiv:2509.22067) and search results report SAE feature steering yields only 1-4% higher compliance than random directions, and a production model was jailbroken via a public SAE steering API. 'Interpretability Tools Are an Attack Channel' (LessWrong).

# Adversarial Suffixes That Hide Activations Defeat Probe Monitors During Jailbreaks

**Problem:** Two failures: (1) activation-probe monitors are evadable via adversarial latent/suffix edits (interp monitoring failure) and (2) adversarial jailbreaks (robustness subfield). The compound: a single optimized suffix can simultaneously jailbreak the model AND suppress the probe's 'unsafe' signal, so the monitor is silent exactly when needed.

**Direction:** Train a simple linear unsafe-content probe on an open model. Using an off-the-shelf prompted-LLM red-teamer (training-free), search for suffixes that both elicit harmful completion and drive the probe below threshold. Measure how often jailbreak success co-occurs with probe evasion vs. independent rates.

**Why it matters:** Probe monitors are promoted as cheap deployment-time guards. Showing that jailbreak and probe-evasion are not independent — that the attack channel for one is the attack channel for the other — directly undercuts the safety case for activation monitoring. Counterfactually valuable, no training.

**Relevant context:** 'Red-teaming Activation Probes using Prompted LLMs' (arXiv:2511.00554) shows training-free black-box attacks on probes; white-box attacks hide unsafe states via adversarial suffixes/latent edits. 'Neural Chameleons' (arXiv:2512.11949) shows models learning to hide thoughts from activation monitors.

# Multi-Directional vs Single-Direction Refusal: Replicating SOM Directions

**Problem:** 'SOM Directions are Better than One' (arXiv:2511.08379) claims multiple refusal directions suppress refusal better than the single Arditi direction. Whether the marginal benefit of extra directions is large or quickly saturates across models is unclear.

**Direction:** On 2 open models, extract the top-k refusal directions (e.g., via difference-in-means across clusters or PCA of harmful-vs-harmless activation differences). Measure refusal-suppression success when ablating 1,2,3,...,k directions and fit a saturation curve. Compare to the single-direction baseline.

**Why it matters:** If refusal is genuinely multi-dimensional, single-direction monitors/defenses are leakier than assumed — important for anyone building cheap direction-based safety tooling outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2511.08379 'SOM Directions are Better than One: Multi-Directional Refusal Suppression'. Arditi et al. single-direction (arXiv:2406.11717). github andyrdt/refusal_direction provides extraction code.

# Cross-Lingual Auto-Interp Failure Amplifies Multilingual Safety Gaps

**Problem:** Compound: (1) SAE auto-interpretation labels degrade in non-English/low-resource languages (interp failure) amplifying (2) the documented multilingual safety gap. If a 'harmful content' SAE feature is correctly labeled in English but mislabeled or missed in another language, any feature-based multilingual safety filter inherits a blind spot exactly where unsafe prompts already evade detection.

**Direction:** Take a multilingual open model with an SAE. Identify a candidate 'toxicity/harm' feature in English. Test its activation and auto-interp label consistency on parallel harmful prompts translated into 3-4 languages (including a low-resource one). Measure the joint gap: feature mislabel rate x baseline safety-filter miss rate per language.

**Why it matters:** Multilingual safety is a real deployed gap that frontier labs deprioritize for low-resource languages. Showing interp-based filters compound rather than fix the gap is high counterfactual value and uses only public translations.

**Relevant context:** 'How Far Do Auto-Interpretation Labels Generalize' (arXiv:2606.00356): features miss meaning in Serbian up to 4x more than English. 'SAEs Can Capture Language-Specific Concepts' (arXiv:2507.11230). XSafety / 'State of Multilingual LLM Safety' (EMNLP 2025) document non-English safety gaps.

# Logit-Lens Unreliability Corrupts Early-Exit / Layer-Skip Safety Decisions

**Problem:** Compound: (1) logit lens basis drift and unfaithfulness at intermediate layers (interp failure) amplifying (2) unsafe early-exit / speculative-decoding deployment decisions (efficiency-safety subfield). If a logit-lens readout is used to decide a token is 'settled' and safe to emit early, basis-drift errors can greenlight harmful tokens that the full forward pass would have suppressed.

**Direction:** On GPT-2/Pythia, compare logit-lens predictions at intermediate layers vs. final output on a set of refusal-triggering prompts. Identify cases where the lens 'predicts' a benign/refusal token mid-stack but the full model emits something different (or vice versa). Estimate the early-exit false-safe rate driven by lens unreliability.

**Why it matters:** Layer-skipping and early-exit are deployed for efficiency. Tying a known interp unreliability to a concrete safety-relevant decision is a fresh angle and fully feasible on small models with no training.

**Relevant context:** Tuned Lens paper (Belrose et al., arXiv:2303.08112): logit lens fails for BLOOM/GPT-Neo, top-1 is often the input token in >half of layers, basis drift causes misaligned intermediate predictions. 'On the Effect of Uncertainty on Layer-wise Inference Dynamics' (arXiv:2507.06722).

# Vision SAE Sparsity Mismatch Amplifies Cross-Modal Jailbreaks

**Problem:** Compound: (1) vision SAEs have very different (higher L0) sparsity structure than language SAEs, so harm features are harder to isolate in the visual stream (interp failure), amplifying (2) the cross-modality alignment gap where image-borne harmful intent evades text-trained safety. A safety feature found in the language side may have no clean visual counterpart.

**Direction:** Using a CLIP SAE (ViT-Prisma / the CLIP-SAE release), attempt to locate a 'harmful concept' feature in the vision encoder analogous to a text harm feature. Measure how monosemantic/isolable it is (L0, top-activating images) versus the language analog, and whether steering it suppresses an image-based jailbreak proxy. Characterize the isolability gap.

**Why it matters:** VLMs are deployed with text-centric safety. Demonstrating that interp tooling is structurally weaker on the visual side — exactly the modality with the alignment gap — is a fresh compound finding. Uses public pre-trained vision SAEs, no training.

**Relevant context:** 'Steering CLIP's vision transformer with SAEs' (arXiv:2504.08729): vision SAE spatial tokens have much higher L0 than CLS/language SAEs. ViT-Prisma provides 80+ pre-trained SAE weights. 'Safe+Safe=Unsafe' (arXiv:2411.11496) and VLM jailbreak surveys (arXiv:2502.14881) document the cross-modality safety gap.

# Probe Spurious Features Plus Sandbagging Hide Capability Concealment

**Problem:** Compound: (1) probing classifiers detecting correlated-but-not-causal features (interp failure) and (2) sandbagging / strategic underperformance (capability-eval subfield). A 'capability present' probe that actually tracks a spurious surface cue can be silenced by a sandbagging model that strips the cue while retaining capability, so the probe under-reports exactly when concealment occurs.

**Direction:** On an open model, build a probe that predicts whether the model 'can' solve a task class from activations. Construct a sandbagging-style prompt that makes the model underperform. Test whether the probe still detects latent capability, and whether the probe's signal was riding on a spurious feature (ablate suspected spurious dims and re-check).

**Why it matters:** Capability probes are pitched as sandbagging detectors. Showing the detector inherits the probe's spurious-correlation weakness — compounding the concealment problem — is a model-organism-flavored, lab-independent study.

**Relevant context:** 'Probing Classifiers are Unreliable for Concept Removal and Detection' (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2207.04153): probes claim concept presence from correlated features. Search results: sandbagging evades simple white-box detection unless elicited by targeted fine-tuning. Open Phil interp benchmark gap.

# Feature Splitting Across SAE Sizes Destabilizes Safety Audits

**Problem:** Compound: (1) feature splitting — a single concept latent fractures into many sub-latents as SAE width grows (interp reliability failure) amplifying (2) audit/governance failure where a 'we monitored the harm feature' safety claim silently breaks when the SAE is swapped or scaled. The audited feature no longer exists as one object.

**Direction:** Take two pre-trained SAEs of different widths for the same model/layer (Gemma Scope offers multiple widths). Pick a safety-relevant concept, find its latent in the small SAE, and trace how it splits in the larger one. Quantify how much a single-feature monitor's coverage drops after splitting, and whether any sub-feature alone reproduces the original detection.

**Why it matters:** Audits and governance increasingly cite 'we watch feature X.' Showing this claim is non-portable across SAE scale/width is a concrete, fresh reliability result feasible with only downloaded weights.

**Relevant context:** 'A is for Absorption' (arXiv:2409.14507) and 'Position: Prioritize Feature Consistency in SAEs' (arXiv:2505.20254) document feature splitting/instability as width grows and note current instability is underestimated. Gemma Scope provides multi-width SAEs.

# Interp-Guided Adversarial Examples Plus Probe Monitoring Collapse

**Problem:** Compound: (1) mech interp used offensively to craft targeted adversarial inputs (interp-as-attack-channel) amplifying (2) the failure of probe-based monitors. If circuit/feature knowledge lets an attacker craft inputs that route around the exact activations a probe watches, interp simultaneously builds the attack and reveals the monitor's blind axis.

**Direction:** On a small open model, train an unsafe-content probe and identify the activation directions it reads. Use simple interp (gradient/feature attribution) to construct prompt perturbations that minimize the probe's read-out while preserving harmful output. Measure attack success enabled specifically by interp knowledge vs. a black-box baseline.

**Why it matters:** Argues a dual-use point: the same interpretability that powers a monitor maps out how to evade it. Quantifying the net effect is counterfactually valuable and needs only one consumer GPU.

**Relevant context:** 'Using Mechanistic Interpretability to Craft Adversarial Attacks' (arXiv:2503.06269). 'Interpretability Tools Are an Attack Channel' (LessWrong). 'Red-teaming Activation Probes using Prompted LLMs' (arXiv:2511.00554) gives a black-box baseline to compare against.

# SAE Error Term Hides Harm When Reconstruction-Based Monitoring Is Used

**Problem:** Compound: (1) SAE reconstruction error / dark-matter (the part of activations SAEs don't explain — an interp completeness failure) amplifying (2) monitoring failure when a system flags inputs only by SAE-feature activations. Harmful computation routed through the un-reconstructed residual is invisible to a feature-based monitor.

**Direction:** On an open model with a pre-trained SAE, compare a harm classifier trained on (a) SAE feature activations vs (b) raw residual-stream activations, on a harmful/benign set. Measure how much detection signal lives in the SAE error term that a feature-only monitor discards. Construct/identify examples detectable in raw but not SAE space.

**Why it matters:** Feature-based monitoring is sold as 'interpretable safety.' Quantifying that a meaningful fraction of harm signal lives in the discarded reconstruction error is a clean, surprising compound result with only public SAEs.

**Relevant context:** DeepMind 'Negative Results for SAEs on Downstream Tasks' (deepmindsafetyresearch Medium) found SAE probes underperform raw-activation probes. Search results: SAEs lack ground truth and have nonlinear error / feature absorption. SAELens pre-trained SAEs available.

# Planning-Ahead Circuits Plus CoT Unfaithfulness Hide Goal-Directedness

**Problem:** Compound: (1) models internally plan ahead (Anthropic found Haiku selects rhyme words before writing the line) yet (2) CoT can be unfaithful. The compound failure: a model can pursue a multi-step internal plan whose existence is invisible both to mechanistic readout (if we only watch the output stream) and to CoT monitoring (if the plan is never verbalized) — a model-organism for unverbalized scheming.

**Direction:** On a small open model, set up a constrained planning task (e.g. forced-rhyme or a two-step puzzle). Use logit-lens/probing on intermediate positions to detect whether a future-token decision is encoded early. Then check whether the CoT mentions that decision. Measure the rate of 'internally planned but not verbalized' cases as a tiny model-organism of hidden planning.

**Why it matters:** Directly probes a >1-year threat model (covert long-horizon goals) on a feasible slice, combining a flagged surprising result with CoT-faithfulness concerns. No training, just probing an existing model.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic Circuit Tracing 'On the Biology of an LLM' (transformer-circuits.pub 2025): Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhyme words ahead. 'Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability' (Barez et al.). TransformerLens supports logit lens / activation capture on small models.

# Auto-Interp Confabulation Plus Automated Auditing Pipelines

**Problem:** Compound: (1) LLM auto-interpretation produces confident but wrong feature labels (interp failure) amplifying (2) automated-auditing pipelines that trust those labels to triage features for safety review. A confabulated 'benign' label causes a genuinely harm-related feature to be auto-dismissed, so automation scales the labeling error into missed audits.

**Direction:** Take a set of pre-labeled SAE features (Neuronpedia / auto-interp outputs). Re-derive labels with a cheap LLM and measure disagreement. For a subset, run a simple ground-truth activation test (does the feature actually fire on its claimed concept?). Estimate the false-benign rate and simulate how many harm features an auto-triage step would discard.

**Why it matters:** Automated interpretability auditing is an emerging agenda. Showing how confabulated labels compound into systematic audit misses is fresh, lab-independent, and uses only public feature dashboards.

**Relevant context:** Search results: auto-interp interpretability scores can be misleading and don't penalize high-frequency uninterpretable latents; SAEs lack ground truth. 'Automated Interpretability-Driven Model Auditing' research agenda (Oxford AIGI, 2026). Neuronpedia hosts auto-interp labels.

# Steering-Induced Capability Damage Plus Silent Safety Regression

**Problem:** Compound: (1) activation/SAE steering distorts hidden representations and degrades general capability (interp-intervention side effect) amplifying (2) a safety regression where the degraded model produces lower-quality but still-harmful outputs that bypass quality-based filters. The interp 'fix' both hurts utility and leaves a residual unsafe channel.

**Direction:** Apply a refusal-steering intervention to an open model. Measure (a) capability drop on a small benchmark, and (b) whether harmful outputs persist but in degraded/obfuscated form that a perplexity or quality heuristic would let through. Map the steering-strength frontier where safety gain is overtaken by capability loss + residual harm.

**Why it matters:** Steering is promoted as a lightweight safety lever. Characterizing the joint capability/safety cost frontier is decision-relevant and fully feasible at small scale without training.

**Relevant context:** 'The Rogue Scalpel' (arXiv:2509.22067): activation steering compromises safety. Search results: inference-time SAE steering distorts hidden representation distributions, limiting utility retention and jailbreak resilience (arXiv:2505.24428). GSAE (arXiv:2512.06655) on distributed safety representations.

# Does Probe Detection Survive Paraphrase but Not Obfuscation?

**Problem:** Activation probes detect 'ordinary jailbreaks' at >=90% recall (arXiv:2601.11516) but collapse under deliberate obfuscated activations (arXiv:2412.09565). The intermediate regime — natural-language paraphrase and translation of harmful requests — is untested and reflects realistic non-adversarial drift.

**Direction:** Train a harmfulness probe on an open model, then evaluate recall on (a) original harmful prompts, (b) LLM-paraphrased versions, (c) translated-then-back-translated versions, (d) explicit obfuscation-suffix attacks. Map the recall degradation gradient from benign drift to active attack.

**Why it matters:** Real deployments face benign distribution shift far more often than active obfuscation. Knowing where probes break under realistic paraphrase informs realistic-threat benchmarking (a core open problem). No training of the base model needed.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2601.11516 (probes fragile to distribution shift). arXiv:2412.09565 (obfuscation defeats probes). Open Problems: 'realistic jailbreak benchmarks reflecting actual attacker capabilities'.

# Probe Layer Choice Instability Plus Distribution Shift at Deployment

**Problem:** Compound: (1) probe performance varies sharply by layer and is unstable (interp reliability failure) amplifying (2) distribution-shift failure at deployment. A probe tuned to its best layer on in-distribution data can collapse on shifted inputs, and the layer that was best in-distribution may be the worst under shift — so the very tuning choice that maximized in-dist accuracy maximizes out-of-dist failure.

**Direction:** Train unsafe-content probes at every layer of a small open model on one harmful-prompt distribution. Evaluate each layer's probe on a shifted distribution (paraphrases, another harm taxonomy). Measure whether best-in-distribution layer ranking inverts under shift, quantifying the compound deployment risk of layer selection.

**Why it matters:** Layer selection is an under-examined free parameter. Showing it interacts adversarially with distribution shift is a fresh, cheap, decision-relevant reliability finding for anyone fielding probe monitors outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** Search results: logit-lens/probe extracted information 'varies from layer to layer.' 'Probing Classifiers are Unreliable' (arXiv:2207.04153). 'Red-teaming Activation Probes' (arXiv:2511.00554) provides shifted adversarial inputs. TransformerLens captures per-layer activations.

# Superposition Plus Concept Erasure Leakage

**Problem:** Compound: (1) superposition packs concepts into overlapping directions (core interp difficulty) amplifying (2) concept-erasure / RMU-style removal failures. If the target concept shares directions with benign concepts due to superposition, erasing it either damages benign behavior or leaves the concept recoverable from the overlap — a guaranteed lose-lose.

**Direction:** On a small open model, pick two concepts known to share representational space. Apply a linear concept-erasure method (e.g. LEACE-style projection, runnable on CPU/GPU). Measure leakage: can a fresh probe recover the 'erased' concept from the residual, and how much collateral damage hits the entangled benign concept? Tie the leakage rate to a superposition overlap metric.

**Why it matters:** Concept erasure is a leading lightweight safety method. Grounding its failures in superposition gives a mechanistic explanation and a measurable risk, all feasible with public tooling and no training.

**Relevant context:** 200 Concrete Open Problems and Toy Models of Superposition (Anthropic) frame superposition. 'Probing Classifiers are Unreliable for Concept Removal' (arXiv:2207.04153) shows erasure leakage. LEACE concept-erasure code is public and lightweight.

# Attribution-Graph Incompleteness Plus Over-Trusted Safety Cases

**Problem:** Compound: (1) attribution graphs / circuit tracing omit a fraction of the true computation (interp completeness failure) amplifying (2) governance failure when a 'we traced the circuit, it's safe' claim is treated as a guarantee. The untraced fraction is exactly where unverified behavior can hide.

**Direction:** On a small model with available transcoders/SAEs, build a partial attribution graph for a specific behavior and measure completeness via ablation: how much of the behavior is explained by the traced nodes vs. the residual? Construct a simple input where the traced circuit predicts one outcome but the full model does another, demonstrating the safety-case gap.

**Why it matters:** Translating mechanistic findings into deployment guarantees is an Open Phil priority. Quantifying the residual-behavior gap operationalizes the interp-to-safety gap as a measurable number, valuable to do outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic 'Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs' (transformer-circuits.pub 2025, methods) notes attribution-graph completeness limits. Open Phil RFP: interp-to-safety gap and benchmarks that test whether findings translate to guarantees. Cross-layer transcoders are partially open.

# Reward-Model Feature Opacity Plus Reward Hacking

**Problem:** Compound: (1) inability to mechanistically interpret reward-model internals (interp gap) amplifying (2) reward hacking in RLHF. If we cannot identify which RM features drive scores, we cannot detect when a policy is exploiting a spurious RM feature, so reward hacking proceeds undiagnosed.

**Direction:** Using an open reward model, probe/SAE its activations to find features correlating with high reward. Construct or sample completions that game a suspected spurious feature (e.g. length, formatting, sycophancy markers). Measure whether the RM's high score is attributable to the spurious feature, and whether interp can flag the hack before it would be caught behaviorally.

**Why it matters:** Reward hacking is a central diffuse-reward safety problem. Probing an open RM with interp tools to surface hackable features is model-organism-style, needs no training, and uses public RMs.

**Relevant context:** 'SAFER: Probing Safety in Reward Models with Sparse Autoencoder' (arXiv:2507.00665) applies SAEs to reward models. Open reward models (e.g. on HuggingFace) are public. Sycophancy/length spurious-reward literature supports the hacking targets.

# Tokenizer Artifacts Plus Feature-Based Harm Detection

**Problem:** Compound: (1) interp features are entangled with tokenization artifacts (e.g. first-letter / token-aligned latents from absorption) (interp failure) amplifying (2) harm-detection evasion via simple tokenization manipulation (spacing, homoglyphs, leetspeak). If harm features are partly tokenization-bound, attackers re-tokenizing a harmful phrase silently switch off the feature monitor.

**Direction:** On an open model + SAE, find a harm/concept feature, then perturb harmful inputs with tokenization tricks (added spaces, unicode lookalikes) that preserve meaning. Measure feature-activation drop vs. semantic preservation (judged cheaply). Quantify how much of the monitor's coverage is tokenization-bound and thus trivially evadable.

**Why it matters:** Connects a documented interp artifact (token-aligned absorbed latents) to a real, cheap jailbreak vector. Fresh combination, fully feasible, no training, no lab data.

**Relevant context:** 'A is for Absorption' (arXiv:2409.14507): token-aligned latents absorb concept directions. Search results: SAE latents underperform on first-letter tasks, showing token-binding. Homoglyph/tokenization jailbreaks are documented in robustness literature.

# Quantization Shifts Features Plus Audited-Model-Differs-From-Deployed-Model

**Problem:** Compound: (1) quantization/distillation moves internal features so interp results don't transfer (interp portability failure) amplifying (2) the deployment gap where the audited full-precision model is not the quantized model users hit. A safety feature validated in fp16 may not exist or may relocate in the int4 deployed variant.

**Direction:** Take an open model in fp16 and a 4-bit quantized version. Find a safety-relevant probe/feature in fp16; test whether the same probe direction still detects the concept in the quantized model. Measure detection degradation and feature drift, quantifying how much an fp16 interp audit over-states safety of the deployed quantized model.

**Why it matters:** Almost all real deployment is quantized, but interp/audits run on full precision. Measuring the audit-to-deployment feature gap is a fresh, practically important compound risk runnable on a single consumer GPU.

**Relevant context:** Search results: 'Position: Prioritize Feature Consistency in SAEs' (arXiv:2505.20254) on feature instability across conditions. Quantization is standard (bitsandbytes int4/int8) on consumer GPUs. TransformerLens / probe tooling supports both precisions.

# Polysemantic Refusal Features Plus Over-Refusal Collateral

**Problem:** Compound: (1) polysemantic 'refusal' features fire on benign content too (interp/superposition failure) amplifying (2) over-refusal / helpfulness degradation. Steering or monitoring on a polysemantic refusal feature both miss-detects benign queries as harmful and, when used to enforce refusal, broadens harmless over-refusal — a safety-usefulness compounding cost.

**Direction:** Identify a candidate refusal feature in an open model + SAE. Characterize its activation across a benign-but-sensitive set (medical, legal, security education). Measure false-positive firing, then test whether amplifying the feature for safety increases over-refusal on the benign set. Quantify the joint harm-miss / benign-block frontier.

**Why it matters:** Over-refusal is a fuzzy, under-measured safety-usefulness tradeoff. Tying it to feature polysemanticity gives a mechanistic, lab-independent measurement using public SAEs.

**Relevant context:** Toy Models of Superposition (Anthropic) on polysemanticity. Search results: GSAE (arXiv:2512.06655) finds safety lives in distributed multi-feature patterns, implying single-feature refusal is polysemantic. Over-refusal benchmarks (e.g. XSTest) are public.

# Probe Calibration Drift Plus Automated Gating Decisions

**Problem:** Compound: (1) interp probes are poorly calibrated (scores don't map to true probabilities — interp failure) amplifying (2) automated gating/escalation systems that threshold probe scores. A miscalibrated probe whose threshold was set on clean data will either flood reviewers (false alarms) or silently pass harm (false negatives) once the input mix shifts.

**Direction:** Train an unsafe-content probe on an open model; produce reliability diagrams on held-out and shifted data. Simulate a gating policy at a fixed threshold and measure how calibration drift changes the realized false-negative/false-positive rates under shift. Report the safety-relevant miscalibration gap.

**Why it matters:** Calibration is rarely reported for safety probes yet determines real gating behavior. A clean, statistics-friendly study (well-matched to the participant's stats skills) that exposes a compound deployment risk without any training or lab data.

**Relevant context:** 'Probing Classifiers are Unreliable' (arXiv:2207.04153) and 'Building Better Deception Probes' (arXiv:2602.01425, aggregation errors) motivate calibration concerns. Reliability-diagram / ECE methods are standard statistics. TransformerLens for activations.

# Hidden-Thought Suppression Plus Latent Monitor Training

**Problem:** Compound: (1) models can learn to hide their thoughts from activation monitors ('Neural Chameleons') amplifying (2) the false confidence created when a latent monitor was validated only against non-evasive models. The compound failure: training/selecting a monitor on cooperative behavior makes deployment teams trust it precisely against the adversarial behavior it cannot see.

**Direction:** Use a published evasion dataset or a simple prompted setup to elicit 'hidden-thought' behavior in an open model. Train a latent monitor on normal data, then evaluate it on the evasive cases. Measure the drop and whether any robust signal survives in deeper/earlier layers. Frame as a small model-organism evaluation of monitor brittleness.

**Why it matters:** Directly engages a >1-year deceptive-alignment threat model on a tractable slice. Counterfactually valuable: evaluating monitor robustness against hidden thoughts needs no lab infra, only an open model and public methods.

**Relevant context:** 'Neural Chameleons: LMs Can Learn to Hide Their Thoughts from Unseen Activation Monitors' (arXiv:2512.11949). 'Red-teaming Activation Probes' (arXiv:2511.00554). Anthropic Auditing Game framing (emergentmind) for model-organism setup.
